1.21.1.0.653.0:
### 0.653.0

**Library rooms have their books back**

Portal library rooms had been turning up with completely bare shelves. They are stocked again — and when nobody has written enough books in your language to fill one, the room now settles for the closest author it can find instead of standing empty. Expect a shorter shelf in that case rather than none at all. A dropped connection to the community book service no longer empties every library in your world for the rest of the session either; a room that comes up short quietly tries again a few minutes later.

- Library rooms are stocked with books again instead of standing bare
- If nobody writes enough in your language, the room picks the closest author it can rather than showing nothing — a shorter shelf you can read beats a full one you cannot
- A hiccup reaching the community book service no longer leaves every library in the world empty until you restart
- A library that finds nobody tries again a few minutes later, so one thin moment no longer settles it
1.21.1.0.652.0:
### 0.652.0

**Jump from a translation to its source**

The translation editor now shows a View source link beside the English heading. It opens a search of the Dungeon Train repository for that string's key, so you can see where the game actually uses the line you are translating.

- View source link on the heading row of the translation editor
- Finds both the English entry and every place the code uses it
1.21.1.0.651.0:
### 0.651.0

**Translation editor explains every variable**

In the translation editor, the placeholders in an English string are now underlined, and hovering one says what the game actually puts there with a few real examples. Where the value is itself a translated phrase, the example is shown in the language you are translating into, with the English beside it.

- Placeholders like %s and %1$s are underlined in the English source
- Hover a placeholder for what it holds, plus two or three real example values
- Examples that are themselves translated show in your language and in English
1.21.1.0.650.0:
### 0.650.0

**Translators can read the whole English string again**

The translation editor used to cut the English off after six lines, so the mod's longest strings — the books — could not be read in full by the person being asked to translate them. Nothing is truncated now: the text grows to fit, scrolls when there is more of it, and the divider between it and your translation can be dragged to give either side more room.

- The English on the translate screen is no longer cut off — it scrolls instead
- Drag the divider to trade room between the original text and your translation
- The "unreviewed machine translation" warning stays visible while you scroll

### 0.649.0

**The vote page lines up with the book again**

After reading a community book, the train's vote page sat in the wrong place — its question could land on top of the "Page 2 of 2" line, and at some window sizes the thumbs drifted off the page entirely and stopped responding where you clicked them. The page now follows the book wherever it sits, including when Scribble's centred book layout moves it.

- The train's question no longer collides with the page counter
- The thumbs and the report button now click where they are drawn, at every window size and GUI scale

**Abandoning a run always shows the recap**

With the Immediate Respawn game rule on, choosing "Abandon This Run" from the pause menu used to drop you straight into a fresh world, skipping the end-of-run recap entirely. Now it takes you to the death screen like any other run ending, so you can read the recap and choose when to board again. Immediate Respawn also carries over into each new world the train makes for you, instead of quietly switching itself off after the first one.

- Abandon This Run now opens the death screen even with Immediate Respawn on
- Dying normally still rolls straight into a fresh world when Immediate Respawn is on
- The Immediate Respawn setting now sticks across every world in a run chain
1.21.1.0.648.0:
### 0.648.0

**The train question now shows up wherever a run starts**

The choice between your own train designs and the built-in ones is now offered on every route that begins a run — including Minecraft's own Create New World screen, which used to ask only after the world had been built. Backing out with Escape returns you to the menu you came from and creates nothing.

- Create New World from the vanilla menu now asks before the world is generated, like Dungeon Train's own New World button does.
- The Train Editor no longer asks. Editor worlds are creative, so they are Free Play anyway and always load your designs.
- Dying with immediate respawn on reuses your last answer instead of interrupting the reboard.
1.21.1.0.647.0:
### 0.647.0

**Choose your train before the world starts**

If you've made your own train designs, Dungeon Train now asks what you want to do the moment you start a run — not after the world has already been built around the answer. Pick Custom Train to play your designs, or Default Train to play the built-in ones with your stats counting as normal.

- The question is asked when you press New World or reboard, so choosing Default Train means a world that never loads the custom content at all.
- Two clear cards instead of a wall of text, with a ? button explaining what Free Play costs.
- The Free Play badge no longer lingers on saves where it no longer applies — it clears itself on your next login.
1.21.1.0.646.0:
### 0.646.0

**A book the train never confirmed is no longer counted twice**

If the train stored your book but the reply never got back to you — a restart, a timeout, a bad connection — your game sends it again, as it always has. That resend was being read as you uploading the same book twice, and it briefly cost four writers an upload pause they had not earned. Each upload now carries a handle the train recognises, so a resend is understood as the same book arriving again rather than a new offence.

- A re-sent upload is recognised as a retry and never counts as a duplicate

### 0.645.0

**The train refuses a book you have already sent**

Send the train the same book twice and it now says no, and stops taking your writing for a while — thirty seconds the first time, doubling with each repeat, up to an hour. While it is refusing you, the Sign button in the book screen turns red and will not press, with the time left on it, so you never burn a book for nothing. Someone else writing out a book they found in loot is not affected: only re-sending your OWN book counts.

- A re-upload of your own book is refused instead of silently ignored
- Uploads pause for 30s, doubling per repeat, capped at an hour and forgotten after a clean week
- The Sign button goes red and dead while paused, and frees itself when the time is up
- Lectern letters, Death Notes and Love Notes are all paused too

**A cat rides the train, and netherite scrap turns up in loot**

Carriages that carried cows may now carry a cat instead — or, rarely, an ocelot. Netherite scrap has also been added to the loot tables.

- New cat carriage content, with a rare ocelot variant
- Netherite scrap added to prefab loot
1.21.1.0.644.0:
### 0.644.0

**Only dimensional carriages take you to their rooms**

An ordinary carriage could send you into a dimensional carriage's room without you ever walking through one. It no longer can.
1.21.1.0.643.0:
### 0.643.0

**Every animal you tame is counted in your death report**

Tame a wolf, a cat, a horse — anything — and it is tallied for the life you are living. When that life ends, the count appears on your death screen and in your death report alongside the rest of the run: how far you got, what you fought, what you carried. A life spent making friends of animals now leaves a mark in the record, not just in the moment.

- Taming anything counts toward the life you are currently living, and resets when you die.
- The tally shows on the in-game death screen and in the Discord death report.

**Your pets come back with your echo**

The animals you tamed are remembered when you die. When an echo of that life returns to the train, up to three of your pets walk back on with it — loyal to the echo exactly as they were to you. They follow it down the carriage, teleport to it when they fall behind, and turn on anyone who attacks it. Mounts stay behind unless you gave them a name: a horse you never named was transport, not a companion.

- Up to three tamed animals return alongside an echo of the life that tamed them.
- They follow, teleport and defend exactly as pets do for a living player.
- Unnamed mounts are left behind; a named one comes back with you.
- Taming counts as kindness, so a life spent befriending animals returns friendlier.
- Requires Interactive Player Mobs 0.92.0 or newer.
1.21.1.0.642.0:
### 0.642.0

**Hand-written lore books can be stocked in train loot chests**

Books written and signed inside an editor plot are now ordinary written books while you build with them — they no longer catch fire when you read or drop them, so you can proof-read one and place it in a carriage's chest. Once that carriage rides the live train, the first player to take the book out of the chest arms it, and it burns after being read like any other book you find out there.

- Books signed in an editor plot no longer burn while you're building
- Authored books can be stocked in a carriage's loot chest and saved into the template
- Found on the live train, they still burn after reading

**Better book writing**

Writing a book in-game is far less painful. The Dungeon Train modpack now bundles Scribble, which adds page insert and delete, undo and redo, and the ability to save a book to a file and load it back later. Books you write still look exactly the same to everyone else, whether or not they have the mod.

- Insert and delete pages anywhere in a book, instead of only adding to the end
- Undo and redo while writing
- Save a book to a file and load it back into a fresh book and quill
- Scribble's colour picker is switched off, so book text stays vanilla black — set colorPickerVisible in your Dungeon Train client config to bring it back

### 0.641.0

**Numbers read correctly in languages that decline them**

Counts in chat and on the death screen now take the grammatical form your language actually wants. Russian says «1 раз», «2 раза», «5 раз» instead of forcing everything into one of two English shapes, and the death-screen epitaph reads «второй, кто пал» rather than «два-й». English was quietly wrong here too — it used to say "the twoth to fall". Languages that don't inflect for number, like Japanese and Chinese, are unaffected.

- Russian and Polish counts decline properly — one, few and many forms, including the teens and the second decade
- Death-screen epitaphs spell real ordinals: «второй, кто пал», "the second to fall"
- Elapsed times, book stats, and shared-carriage death lines all follow the reader's own language

**Saving a train package no longer loses your work**

Saving in the Train Editor's Packages menu is now purely additive — it never deletes or moves anything you have built. Edits you make after saving a package now land in that package, so they stick.

- Saving under a new name makes a copy; the package you saved from stays exactly where it was, along with its .zip snapshot.
- Your first save copies your in-progress work into the new package instead of moving it, leaving the originals in place as a backup.
- Portal room, tunnel, track and pillar edits — including removing a block variant — are now written into the package you have active, instead of silently going somewhere the game was not reading.
- Saving over a package name that only exists as a .zip is now refused rather than overwriting that .zip.
- If a save cannot finish, your previous snapshot is left untouched instead of being deleted first.
- The Packages menu now shows Save only on the active package's row, so it can no longer look like it will save a different one.
- The custom train content prompt no longer appears when your run is already Free Play, where it had nothing left to ask.
1.21.1.0.640.0:
### 0.640.0

**Modpack releases stop silently going missing from CurseForge**

The CurseForge modpack is published from a manifest that points at that release's Dungeon Train file. If CurseForge has not approved that file yet, it rejects the whole pack — quietly, after the upload looked fine. The release pipeline now waits for the file to actually be approved before building the pack, and stops with a clear reason if it never is, instead of shipping nothing and reporting success.

- Pack uploads no longer reference an unapproved mod file
- A stuck release fails loudly instead of going silently missing

**Find your language, and ask for one that isn't there**

The language list has a search box and a filter, every language can now be translated instead of only the nineteen we ship, and translators who volunteered since the last release are named in the credits.

- Search the language list by name, by country, or by locale code — in your own language or in English. "French", "Französisch", "Germany" and "Switzerland" all find what you would expect, and one country brings up every language spoken there.
- A filter beside the search: all languages, ones with machine translation still waiting on a human, ones a person has been through, and ones with no translation at all.
- The translation editor opens on ANY language, not just the ones Dungeon Train ships. Every line is listed, blank where nothing has been translated yet — including book prose, which was previously invisible if a language had never touched it.
- No machine translation for your language? A button asks for one, and shows how many other players have asked for the same.
- Credits now name every translator whose work has been approved, not only those whose work had shipped when the build was made.
1.21.1.0.639.0:
### 0.639.0

**Library rooms stock authors you can read**

A library portal room fills its shelves with one community author's whole catalogue — and now it only ever picks somebody writing in your game's language. Play in 中文 and the room is a Chinese author's library; play in English and it is an English one. When nobody writes in your language yet, the room falls back to an English author rather than standing empty.

- Author libraries are chosen in your language, not just filtered afterwards
- The book count on the room's author is now the count in your language
- Your own library room still shows everything you have written, in any language

### 0.638.0

**Dimensional carriages, and more of them in Creative**

The room between a portal's two corridors is now called a dimensional carriage in-game, matching what the notes have been calling it. In Creative they arrive on an exact beat — every 5 carriage groups — instead of at random, so you always know where the next one is. Survival is unchanged. Set the rate for a world with /dungeontrain portal carriage <n>; doing so puts the world into Free Play.

### 0.637.0

**Translation editor keeps your search, and its scrollbars work**

Opening a string in the translation editor no longer wipes what you typed in the search box or your place in the list — both are still there when you come back. The editor's two lists also have working scrollbars now: clicking or dragging the bar scrolls, instead of selecting the row hiding behind it.

- Search text and scroll position survive opening a string
- Scrollbars are clickable and draggable in both the strings list and the sent column

### 0.635.0

**Dimensional carriage libraries follow your network-access choice**

A dimensional carriage that stocks its shelves from your own writing has to ask the server which books are yours, which means sending your player ID. It now does that only if you allowed network access; if you declined, the carriage stocks from another player's library instead.
1.21.1.0.634.0:
### 0.634.0

**Reset your progress**

A Reset Everything button on the Video Tools page. Wipes your advancements, stats, story progress, Ender Chest and past lives, and deletes your Dungeon Train worlds, so the game treats you as a first-time player again.

- Names every world it will delete and makes you type DELETE first — there is no undo
- Worlds without Dungeon Train in them are left alone
1.21.1.0.633.0:
### 0.633.0

**Blocks left outside a template plot show up red**

Only what sits inside a plot is saved into the template. Anything outside it now wears a red ghost, from anywhere in the editor.
1.21.1.0.632.0:
### 0.632.0

**Custom train content now asks before it changes your run**

If you've built your own carriages in the Train Editor — or installed someone else's pack — starting a world now asks what you want to do with them. Continue and you play with your creations, but the run counts as Free Play: it won't add to your profile or global stats. Disable them and the world runs the built-in designs, and your stats count as normal. Tick 'Remember decision' and it won't ask again; you can change your mind any time in Options, or with /customcontent.

- A prompt at the start of any world running custom train content, with Continue / Disable Custom Changes and a Remember decision checkbox.
- Playing with custom content is Free Play — advancements still earn live, but they don't count towards your profile or global totals.
- Disabling is per-world and reversible: the world falls back to the built-in designs, and /customcontent on brings yours back.
- A new Custom Train Content row in Options -> Dungeon Train sets what happens by default.

**Move, turn and mirror a whole template in the editor**

The train editor can now rearrange the plot you are standing in, instead of you rebuilding it block by block. Offset slides the build and wraps it at the plot edges, rotate turns it, and flip mirrors it — and any of the three is a single Ctrl+Z away from being undone.

- /dt editor offset <x> <y> <z> slides the build, wrapping at the plot faces so nothing is lost
- /dt editor rotate 90|180|270 turns the build; a quarter turn needs a square plot, so carriages take 180
- /dt editor flip x|y|z mirrors the build, vertical flips included
- Variant pools, lock groups and container loot pools travel with the blocks — the build stays wired up
1.21.1.0.631.0:
### 0.631.0

**See how your own books are landing**

The last page of a book you wrote now shows its thumbs up and thumbs down count. The numbers refresh whenever you pick the book up.

- Vote counts sit where the voting buttons are on other people's books — yours report, they don't ask.
- A released book of yours shows its tally even at zero, so "nobody has voted yet" is something you can actually see.

**Portal room variety restored**

Since v0.630.0 portal rooms had been coming up as libraries far more often than intended, and those libraries always drew from your own shelf instead of mixing in other writers. Test settings had been shipped as real content by mistake. The original room weights are back.

- Libraries are rare again, and the rooms you meet are varied again.
- Library rooms go back to mostly showing other people's writing, with your own as the occasional treat.
1.21.1.0.630.0:
### 0.630.0

**Find the books you wrote, even the ones the train hasn't let out**

Your own library rooms now stock the books you wrote that the train is still deciding about — or has decided against. Open one and its last page tells you where it stands, in the train's own words. You can also take one of your released books back out of circulation whenever you like.

- Books you wrote that are pending, undecided or refused now appear on your own library shelves instead of vanishing the moment you sign them.
- The last page of one of your books says where it stands: still being read, undecided, or turned away — in orange, or red once it is a no.
- Made Private: take one of your released books off the line so only you can find it. Reversible — the padlock shows what it will do before you click it.
- Protest a verdict you disagree with, on a book the train has actually read. It asks a person to look again; it does not overturn anything by itself.
- No thumbs on a book you wrote — rating your own work was never the point, and it skewed which books everyone else was shown.

### 0.629.0

**Changed settings now show at launch, with one-click restore**

Dungeon Train's difficulty settings are what your advancements and lifetime stats are measured against, so a world running with them changed now plays in Free Play — the same rule that already applied to Adventure Item Stats. If your settings differ, the game tells you on the title screen, lists exactly what changed, and offers to put them back. Your own settings are always backed up first, never deleted, so you can rename a file back to restore them. Settings that don't affect balance — visual options, Discord and telemetry toggles, and the content filters — are unaffected.

- Changed difficulty settings are shown at launch, not discovered mid-run
- One-click restore to defaults, with your old settings kept as backups
- Keeping your changes is remembered, so you're only asked again if something else changes
- New /fixconfig command does the same restore from in-game
1.21.1.0.628.0:
### 0.628.0

**Flag a cheat mod from the death screen**

The Mod Recommendations page now works both ways. Alongside recommending a mod to the creator, each of your installed mods carries a small warning icon — click it to flag that mod as a cheat or hack, say what it lets you do, and send. Flagged mods sink to the bottom of the grid with a warning mark, the way recommended ones keep their tick.

- Report any installed mod as a cheat or hack, with a reason
- Recommendations are unchanged — the tile body still recommends
1.21.1.0.627.0:
### 0.627.0

**Endless portal rooms no longer vanish under other players**

In multiplayer, the endless portal rooms only followed one player — usually the host. Anyone else could watch the floor disappear from around them and drop out of the world, and the room stopped growing ahead of them. Every player in the room now gets their own window of rooms.

- The floor around you is never cleared while you are standing near it, whoever else is in the room
- The room keeps building ahead of every player exploring it, not just the first one in
- Extra corridors are held open the same way, so the way back does not disappear behind you

### 0.626.0

**Version number now shown on the pause menu**

The Dungeon Train version line that sits in the corner of the main menu now also appears on the pause menu, so you can check which build you are on without leaving your run. It carries the same update notice as the title screen — if a newer release is out, the line turns amber and clicking it opens the download page for wherever you installed the mod.

- Version number added to the pause (Esc) menu, matching the main menu
- Shows the same clickable 'update available' notice as the title screen
- Visible in multiplayer as well as singleplayer
1.21.1.0.625.0:
### 0.625.0

**Dimensional carriages can stand under their own sky**

A dimensional carriage's template now chooses the sky it stands under — ordinary daylight, daylight that follows the world clock, or a Nether or End cast. The light eases in as you step inside and eases back out as you leave for the corridor home. The mini-world carriage is the first to use it.

- The mini-world dimensional carriage is now daylit
- Room builders get a Sky control in the dimensional carriage editor
- Turn it off server-wide with the new portalRoomDaylight setting

### 0.624.0

**Edible backpacks are findable again**

Edible backpacks turn up in loot chests, iron/gold chests, decorated pots and the starter chest at their original rates again.

### 0.622.0

**Sable updated to 2.0.5**

Dungeon Train now runs on Sable 2.0.5, which fixes several upstream crashes — most notably a panic when you close the CurseForge or Modrinth launcher before entering a world. Sable is a required download, so update it too.

- Fixes the crash from closing the launcher before joining a world
- Requires Sable 2.0.5 — the modpack updates it for you

**Carriages no longer shift when their blocks change**

Blowing up or mining blocks on a carriage could shove the whole carriage sideways, and the shift survived a save and reload. Beds in the Nether and End were the loudest case, but creepers, trap TNT and ordinary mining did it too.

**Endless plains can have a different floor and roof**

A repeating plain's floor and roof are now set separately in the editor, and either one can be air.

**The deserter's hall by MacaroniWithTheMayonnaise**

A new portal room behind house doors: a spruce hall built by MacaroniWithTheMayonnaise, with the deserter's journal still inside.

- Built by MacaroniWithTheMayonnaise

### 0.621.0

**Undo and redo in the train editor**

The in-world editor now has an undo history on Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Y (Cmd+Z / Cmd+Y on Mac), with an Undo | Redo row in the editor's X menu. It covers block edits, whole-plot actions like Clear and Reset, block variants, and menu changes such as weights, stage links, loot tables and part assignments. Undo works from anywhere — change something, walk away, and you can still take it back.

- Ctrl/Cmd+Z and Ctrl/Cmd+Y, rebindable from the vanilla Controls screen
- Blocks, whole-plot Clear and Reset, block variants, and menu changes all undo
- A mirrored edit undoes as one step, not one per reflected cell
- Broken containers come back with their contents intact
- Works from anywhere, not just while standing in the plot

### 0.620.0

**JEI, ready to switch on**

The modpack now ships Just Enough Items, off by default. Tick it on at install for recipe and item lookup — press R on any item to see how it's made.

- Bundled with the modpack, switched off by default.
1.21.1.0.619.0:
### 0.619.0

**Three weeks of new text, now in all 19 languages**

Everything added since early August was English-only outside en_us — the seven new advancements, the Video Tools page, the skybox blocks, the difficulty-change warning, the drifting-carriage death lines, the community-book report button and more. All of it is now translated into every language Dungeon Train ships in, along with ten in-world books that had never been localized. Machine-translated and marked as such, so the in-game translation editor lists them for human review.

- 115 newly translated interface lines in each of the 19 languages
- Ten new books — including The Drifting Carriages and the cursed and loved starting books — now read in your language
- New Quiet Rules and Train Glossary entries translated to match the English originals

### 0.618.0

**CurseForge modpack keeps up with releases again**

The CurseForge modpack had quietly stopped updating — it sat on v0.592.0 while the mod shipped v0.613.0, because CurseForge was accepting our uploads and then rejecting them behind the scenes with no error anywhere we could see. Uploads now retry when the platform hiccups, and every upload is checked afterwards to confirm it actually went live, so the pack can't silently fall behind again.

- CurseForge modpack is publishing again
- Failed uploads retry instead of losing that version
- A pack version that never goes live now fails loudly

### 0.617.0

**Reviewers can reply to translators, and translators can retire good AI lines**

The in-game translation editor now carries a conversation. When a reviewer turns down a translation you sent, they can say why — and that reply comes back to your client, marked against the line it is about, readable in the list and above the box when you open it, with a note on the title screen when something new is waiting. And when a machine-translated line is already correct, you can now say so: 'Good As Is' retires it from your queue so it stops coming back, and you can put it back at any time.

- Reviewers can reply to a translation, and the reply reaches the translator's client
- A title-screen note tells you when a reviewer has written back
- 'Good As Is' retires a machine-translated line that needs no fixing — reversible, and per install

### 0.616.0

**Endless Open rooms can repeat a single block variant**

An endless open portal room can now be set to repeat one block instead of the room you arrived in — an open plain of sandstone, or of a mix you build yourself. The room you walk into keeps everything its author built; only the ground stretching away from it goes uniform. The block can be a full block variant, with weights, facings and even gaps, authored in the same block-variant menu the rest of the editor uses.

- Copies: a new Single option for Endless Open rooms
- Repeat one block, or a whole block variant with weights and facings
- Air in the variant leaves gaps in the plain
- The default portal room now opens onto a lit plain of shroomlight and blackstone

### 0.615.0

**Bilibili link for Chinese-language players**

Playing in Chinese? There's now a Bilibili button on the main menu, just above Discord — Discord doesn't work in mainland China, so that one was a dead end. It only shows up on Chinese-language clients; everyone else's menu is unchanged.

- New Bilibili button on the main menu, above Discord
- Shows only on Chinese-language clients (简体中文, 繁體中文, 文言文)
- Discord stays where it is — the Bilibili link is added, not swapped in

### 0.614.0

**Portal corridor loot variety**

Chests in a portal's corridors now roll different contents from portal to portal, instead of the same ones every time.
1.21.1.0.613.0:
### 0.613.0

**Villager trade tweaks**

Adjusted what villagers pay for a few items in the Trade Anything slot.

**Player heads remember who died there**

The player heads scattered through the train are no longer anonymous. Each one now wears the face and name of a real player whose run ended at that same carriage — the fourth carriage remembers people who fell in a fourth carriage. Mine one and the head keeps them, so you can carry a fallen traveller with you or set them up somewhere of your choosing.

- Heads in carriage N show players who died at carriage N
- A mined head keeps its face and name, and can be placed anywhere
- Falls back to the bundled skins when there is nobody to remember yet
1.21.1.0.612.0:
### 0.612.0

**Using a creative mod asks first**

Using WorldEdit or Effortless Building now asks whether you want to enter Free Play, the same way switching to Creative does. Decline and nothing happens. Having them installed changes nothing on its own.

- Ordinary building with Effortless Building is still normal play

### 0.611.0

**WorldEdit available in the modpack**

The modpack now ships WorldEdit as an optional extra. It's switched off by default — tick it on in the launcher's optional-mods list if you want an in-game map editor for building. Best used off the moving train: WorldEdit's block edits aren't aware of the train's physics sub-level.

- WorldEdit bundled in the modpack, off by default
- Enable it from the optional-mods list in the CurseForge/Modrinth launcher

### 0.610.0

**Open-plain portal rooms can vary their floor**

Endless Open portal rooms can now reroll their floor and ceiling per tile instead of repeating one pattern to the horizon.

### 0.609.0

**Report a community book**

Community books written by other players now carry a report button beside the thumbs up and down. A thumbs down says a book was weak; reporting says it should not be in the pool at all. Enough reports, relative to how many people have read it, pull the book from circulation and put it in front of a human.

- A report icon sits under the thumbs on the train's question page, on player-written books only
- It takes two clicks — the first arms it, the second sends — and there is no hotkey, so a slip cannot report a book
- Reporting does not cast a vote; the two are separate verdicts
- Reports are weighed against readers, so a well-read book is not pulled by a handful of complaints

### 0.608.0

**Community books can't break your game — and can still be styled**

Books written by other players are now cleaned up before they reach you. Certain characters could previously hide text on a page or stack accent marks until it overflowed, and an emoji landing in exactly the wrong spot in a long title could crash the game outright. That's all handled now, on the server and in the mod. Colour codes and right-to-left writing still work exactly as they did — the cleanup is aimed at characters that do nothing but cause trouble. Ordinary books are unaffected.

- Colour and style codes still work in your book's pages — they're only stripped from titles and author names, where they leaked out into chat and tooltips
- Invisible padding characters are removed from titles, authors and pages; right-to-left writing and emoji sequences are left alone
- An emoji in a long title or a full page can no longer crash the game
- Books already in the community pool are cleaned as they're handed out — nothing needed re-uploading
1.21.1.0.607.0:
### 0.607.0

**Edible backpacks come from loot tables only**

Edible backpacks were being swapped into 1.5% of every loot slot in the game, on top of the chests and pots that were meant to carry them. That global substitution is gone — backpacks now turn up only where the loot tables actually list them, so finding one means something again.

- Edible backpacks no longer replace random items in unrelated containers
- Backpacks still appear in the loot chests, iron/gold chests and decorated pots that list them
1.21.1.0.606.0:
### 0.606.0

**Immediate Respawn now rolls straight into a new run**

Turn on Minecraft's Immediate Respawn game rule and dying skips the death screen entirely — the world is discarded and a fresh Dungeon Train run starts on the spot, the same reboard the death screen's "Board anew" button performs. Previously the rule dropped you back into the world you had just died in, the one way a run could outlive your death. Multiplayer is unchanged: on a server you do not host, Immediate Respawn still respawns you as vanilla does.

- Immediate Respawn ends the run and starts a new world, no button press
- Holding Shift while you die keeps the current game mode, as on the reboard chip
- Remote servers keep vanilla Immediate Respawn behaviour
